sections.html: Highlands County is large and mostly rural, with about 113,000 parcels on the roll and more than 24,000 homestead exemptions in force. Farmland, groves and pasture make up much of the acreage, so a parcel with agricultural use gets treated differently from a house on a town lot. The tax collector serves residents from offices in Sebring and Avon Park, and the Highlands County Tax Collector site carries the payment pages and deadline lists referred to below.

sections.h2: When is Highlands County property tax due?
sections.html:
The collector mails bills by October 31 and starts taking payment in November. The whole amount is due by March 31, and an account that is unpaid or lacks a March 31 postmark turns delinquent on April 1, when interest and fees start to build.

The early payment discount steps down from four percent in November to three, two and one percent in the following months, ending in February. Highlands taxes are paid in arrears, covering the calendar year from January through December. At a closing that means the seller owes a share of a year whose bill the buyer will receive.

  • Installment plan: apply by April 30 for the next tax year. Payments fall in June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (final, no discount).
  • Missed first payment: an account with no first installment by July 31 is dropped from the plan and receives a full bill in October.
  • Homestead deferral: file by January 31 to use the deferral program.

Dates run from the January 1 valuation to the April 1 delinquency, and a few of them catch sellers off guard.

Highlands County property tax calendar
MonthWhat happens
January 31Homestead tax deferral filing deadline
March 1New homestead exemption and agricultural classification applications due
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
April 30Installment plan applications due
On or before June 1Tax certificate sale
AugustTRIM notices mailed
October 31Bills mailed

During May, delinquent real estate accounts are advertised three times in a local newspaper. Delinquent tangible personal property accounts are advertised once.

File a new homestead exemption with the Highlands County Property Appraiser by March 1. It costs nothing for a qualified owner and can be completed in minutes, either at the office or at visits the appraiser makes to municipal sites around the county.

New owners sometimes get mail offering to cut their taxable value for a fee. The appraiser's office points out that those offers sell the same savings the homestead exemption already provides, and that the paid service is generally just instructions on how to apply.

Agricultural land follows a separate path. The application goes to the appraiser before March 1 of the tax year, and only land used in good faith for commercial agriculture qualifies. After approval the classification renews yearly. A house on the parcel does not disqualify the land, but the home site is assessed at just value. Citrus is valued by variety, and the office adjusts assessments after disease or freeze damage cuts production. It stays out of groves because of disease concerns.

Petition the Value Adjustment Board before the deadline printed on your TRIM notice. The petition must be notarized and carries a $50 filing fee for each parcel. The board consists of three county commissioners and two school board members, and it usually appoints special masters, independent of the appraiser's office, to hear the cases.

  • On a value dispute, bring sales of comparable properties from the prior year, before January 1, or an appraisal.
  • On a denied exemption, show that you qualified as of January 1.
  • The board cannot lower a bill because of hardship or because the value rose from last year.
  • A petitioner who loses may sue in circuit court under section 194.171.

The board's clerk mails the written decision within 20 days of the ruling. Millage comes from the county, the cities, the school board and the water management districts, so neither the board nor the appraiser can change a rate. A household that cannot absorb an increase may qualify for a deferral or the installment plan through the tax collector.

sections.h2: What happens if Highlands County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Once the newspaper notices have run, an unpaid account goes into a tax certificate sale held by June 1. The certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years from delinquency, and no later than seven years after the certificate was first issued.

Interest on the applicant's side runs at 1.5 percent a month, starting the month after the application and continuing until the account is redeemed or sold. The applicant is not guaranteed the property. The Highlands County Clerk of Courts schedules and runs the sale. State rules send a homestead certificate under $250 to the county instead of auction, and the opening bid at a homestead deed sale includes half of the last assessed value.

A seller with a certificate on the parcel can still close. Paying it off from proceeds redeems the lien before any deed application is filed.

Order a payoff figure before you list, and find out whether this year's bill has been issued. Bills go to the owner of record, and the recorded deed is what puts the new owner on the appraiser's roll.

The appraiser's database leaves out special assessments such as solid waste collection and fire or road improvement districts, yet those charges appear on the tax bill. Only the tax collector can give you the complete bill with non-ad valorem charges included. If you are splitting a lot or merging parcels, a survey is needed, all taxes on the parcels must be paid, and a mortgage holder must approve in writing.

The state deed stamp tax is 70 cents for each $100 paid. A change of ownership returns a capped assessment to just value on the next January 1. For a current millage figure, read your TRIM notice or ask the appraiser.

Some routine steps save time. Bring the parcel number and a copy of your deed when you contact the offices. Ask the title company to confirm that every earlier tax year is paid. If you are enrolled in the installment plan, list the payments you have made so the closing agent can divide the year correctly. When back taxes would hold up a buyer who depends on a mortgage, a cash purchase has no lender underwriting to wait for, and the title company can settle the balance from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When is Highlands County property tax due?
faqs.a: The full bill is owed by March 31, and April 1 marks delinquency. Bills are mailed October 31, and the discount begins at 4 percent in November and drops a point each month to 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: How do I join the Highlands County installment plan?
faqs.a: Send an application to the tax collector by April 30 for the coming tax year. Payments fall in June, September, December and March, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three and none on the last.

faqs.q: What is the filing deadline for a Highlands County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: March 1, with the Highlands County Property Appraiser. Filing is free for qualified owners, and the office advises ignoring paid mailers that offer to reduce taxable value for a fee.

faqs.q: Can I petition the Value Adjustment Board in Highlands County?
faqs.a: Yes, before the deadline on your TRIM notice. The petition is notarized and costs $50 per parcel, and hardship or a rise in value from last year is not enough on its own to win a reduction.

faqs.q: Who runs the Highlands County tax deed sale?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Courts schedules and conducts it. A certificate holder applies through the tax collector's vendor once two years have run from the date of delinquency, and the holder is not guaranteed to get the property.
